record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends George Robert Gray proofs for Birds and the Natatores manuscript, asking for general observations and checks of French and Latin passages. The retained HTML body is a bracketed editorial description with short quoted phrases, so its paraphrase is not treated as verbatim Darwin prose.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day [4 Dec 1838], within period; the date is supported by the 6 December Gray letter footnote but remains editorially supplied.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: The source record is addressed to George Robert Gray. The body preserves quoted Darwin phrases inside an editorial bracketed description; the manuscript/proofs are enclosures or referenced materials.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later outgoing Darwin proof letter to the same Gray, but no surviving Gray response and no response arrow between two outgoing records.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No surviving Gray input is in the corpus; this initiates or continues a proof exchange but cannot be paired to another outgoing Darwin record. No surviving direct input is located; the bracketed body supports the proof/manuscript request but not a full literal transcript.

evidence.quote: I am ashamed of my work, but I cannot do it better
if you would compare the French sentence at p. 20 with M. D’Orbigny’s work
the manuscript of the ‘Natatores’

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends additional Birds proofs to George Robert Gray, asks Gray to check Latin accents, and says these pages complete the next number.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied single XML day [6 Dec 1838], within period; the footnote derives the likely day from the Thursday header and the Birds context.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to George Robert Gray; proof sheets are the object of the request.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Two days earlier, same proof project and Gray, but both are outgoing Darwin letters and no Gray reply survives.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: A continuation/request in the same proof exchange, not a surviving response to an incoming Gray letter. No incoming Gray text is present; same-topic proximity to 451 is insufficient for a direct pair.

evidence.quote: I send you a few more pages of the Proofs
Will you see whether the latin adverbs are properly accented

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Gray to return Merulidae/Anthus skins and a stuffed Upucerthia, records his doubts about Anthus species and Falkland Emberiza specimens, and supplies catalogue/locality and shooting-month notes.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [June–Oct 1839] (1839-06-01 through 1839-10-31); exact day and internal order are unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to G. R. Gray. The specimens and catalogue extracts are Darwin’s information; the requested skins/specimen are physical materials, not an enclosed letter.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Gray proof work, but no specimen or Anthus material overlap sufficient to make a reply.
Later Gray exchange about Birds production, but no surviving Gray response and no unique textual continuation.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Asks for materials and supplies observations in an ongoing ornithological exchange; no surviving Gray input is identified. The date range and shared Birds topic do not identify a particular antecedent Gray letter.

evidence.quote: the skins of the Merulidæ Anthus
the stuffed specimen of Upucerthia
I put mark of ? to 1923 whether different species or not

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson answers Darwin’s questions on elevation and depression. He weighs shells, alluvium, coral and coast formation across Malacca, Coromandel, Arabia, Bombay, Java and related localities; cites many published authorities; identifies specimens held by Sowerby and the Geological Society; and closes with local geological leads and a request for future questions.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 24 July 1839. The date is explicit; it dates Malcolmson’s response, not Darwin’s unlocated prompt or Darwin’s receipt of this letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes all surviving prose. Quotations from Ward, Low and other publications are embedded third-party text; specimens and cited papers are evidence/routes, not Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Later Malcolmson letter says it answers a later/last Darwin letter and also distinguishes a former letter; it cannot be the antecedent of this 24 July response.
Later continuation of geological correspondence, but incoming-to-incoming sequence does not identify the missing Darwin prompt.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Direct reply to an unlocated Darwin letter/questions is explicit, but no matching Darwin source survives in this corpus. The body says “answer your letter” and “your questions”, but the prompt text and actual receipt date are absent; publication references cannot substitute for it.

evidence.quote: answer your letter
a very hurried answer to your questions
If you write soon direct to me “Post Office Edinburgh”

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson explains delayed replies, distinguishes Darwin’s former and last letters, discusses the Glen Roy theory, then supplies extensive Arabia observations: saline plains, conglomerates, coral and shell beds, Kamran’s raised coral cliffs, Aden and Jedda.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 31 August 1839; explicit date for the incoming letter. Its references to earlier/later Darwin papers do not date receipt of those materials.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes; Mr Anderson, McCulloch, Lonsdale, Sowerby and other authorities are reported or quoted as third-party evidence. The body ends mid-sentence and is incomplete.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier Malcolmson incoming letter on related coastal geology, but it is not Darwin’s “former” or “last” letter and cannot be used as an antecedent.
Later Malcolmson incoming letter on related topics; the sequence is thematic and does not establish which Darwin letter is answered.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Incoming response to one or more unlocated Darwin letters; it does not supply a Darwin prompt and its missing ending limits scope. Distinct wording proves unlocated Darwin correspondence (“your letter”, “your former letter”, “your last letter”), but no Darwin ID is available; “not yet received your paper from London” is a paper, not a surviving letter pair.

evidence.quote: I found I had taken your former letter by mistake
Before I got your last letter
I have not yet received your paper from London

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson relays Allan’s unresolved Aldabra view, transcribes Hardie’s Macclesfield Bank sounding and coral fragments, offers sand, discusses trout dissections with Shier and Agassiz, describes grooved sandstone and submarine peat, and challenges Darwin’s erratic-block theory before asking him to write.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 7 October 1839. The date is explicit; “expecting the Voyages” and awaiting Darwin’s paper indicate correspondence state but not actual receipt of a particular missing letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes. The long Hardie quotation, Allan’s views, Agassiz conversation and cited works are third-party information; specimens/sand and printed memoirs are physical or publication routes.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Prior Malcolmson incoming on Arabia and Glen Roy; no direct Darwin prompt is preserved and the subject overlap is insufficient.
Editorially placed after this letter because of the Journal expectation, but it is a separate incoming comment and has a held broad date.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Responds to unlocated Darwin inquiries and theory; p1 says Allan has Darwin’s last letter, but neither that letter nor an Allan response survives here. Topic continuity and the editorial footnote do not identify the missing Darwin source; publication and manuscript expectations are not receipt evidence.

evidence.quote: Dr Allan has got your last letter
I take advantage of an opportunity to send you all Dr. Hardie says of the Mecclesfield Bank
a difficulty to your erratic block theory

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson comments on Darwin’s published Journal of researches discussion of erratic blocks, correcting or extending references to Jameson, Agassiz and Jura geology, describing grooved sandstone at Pettycur, and rejecting glacier explanations for familiar Scottish drift.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held ambiguous bounded range: [after 7 Oct 1839] (XML 1839-10-08 through 1882-12-31), with an editorial date based on the assumption that Malcolmson received/read the Journal soon after 7 October. The hold remains because the source itself supplies no exact day or upper contemporary bound.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes; the body is a surviving fragment, not a complete letter. References to Journal page numbers and published authorities are not Darwin voice.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: The editorial dating assumption uses 535’s statement that the Journal was expected, but this is not a direct reply link.
Later Malcolmson letter discusses the Glen Roy paper and drift, but it is not the same publication-comment fragment.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Comment on a published Darwin work, with no surviving direct Darwin prompt or response pair. Its editorial date is an assumption from expected/read publication timing; it must not be promoted to a secure contemporary day. The final “from the west” passage is the surviving end, while the document may omit other material.

evidence.quote: The shores of the Tertiary sea of the Jura
the sandstones having grooved and polished surfaces exactly like the limestone of Neuchatel
can hardly be explained by the theory of glaciers

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson sends a coralline specimen with worm-bored grooves and explains his observations of Nereis borings in raised-beach and recent limestone. He reports Allan’s Aldabra/Comoros views and promised coral-growth experiments, offers Indian specimens and fossil localities, and asks Darwin to forward a packet to Royle.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 30 November 1839. This dates Malcolmson’s letter and specimen dispatch, not the arrival of the specimen or Allan’s promised letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes. The coralline, worms, possible Kunkar/Laterite samples and packet are physical objects/routes; Allan, Fleming, Miller, Johnston and Owen are reported third parties.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier incoming letter also mentions Allan, coral and Darwin’s Journal; no unique Darwin prompt or response text survives.
Shares Darwin’s published geology topic, but publication comments are not a direct correspondence antecedent.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Incoming specimen/report with offers and forwarding instructions; no surviving Darwin reply or prompt is located. The offer to send specimens and Allan’s promised letter establish material/information routes, not a Darwin voice or receipt of a particular enclosure.

evidence.quote: I take advantage of a young friend going to London to send you a specimen of a coralline
Allan promised to write you a long letter
Please to send the packet to Royle over from the Geol. anytime you are there

record_reviews.summary: Malcolmson recommends Robertson for Geological Society membership, thanks Darwin for the Glen Roy paper, relays Stables’s observations of parallel roads, argues that Scottish drift and terraces are marine, and invites Darwin to inspect Scottish sites. The surviving letter is incomplete.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Safe single XML day 2 January 1840. The day is explicit for the incoming letter; footnote says the final part is missing and the final paragraph is written above the salutation.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Malcolmson writes; Stables, Fleming, Murchison, Lonsdale and other voices are reported. Robertson’s certificate is an enclosure, and the missing ending limits the surviving scope.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Footnote cross-reference and shared Glen Roy/erratic topics, but no direct reply text identifies 535 as the prompt.
Both concern drift/blocks, but 559 comments on a published Journal and has a held date; no direct pair.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Acknowledges receipt and reading of Darwin’s Glen Roy paper and proposes a Geological Society certificate; no surviving Darwin letter is identified. Receipt of the Glen Roy paper is explicit, but it is a paper and not necessarily a letter. No Darwin response survives; the final portion is missing.

evidence.quote: put your name to the enclosed certificate
I have to thank you for your most interesting paper on Glen Roy, which I read with great interest
examine the terraces on the side of the vale of Rothes

record_reviews.summary: Darwin thanks Gray for his volume of Genera of Birds and presses him to finish Gould’s remaining Birds of Beagle’s Voyage manuscript, explaining that illness delayed Darwin’s own work.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [20 Nov–11 Dec 1840] (1840-11-20 through 1840-12-11); exact day unresolved despite the 12 Upper Gower Street header.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to George Robert Gray. Gray’s volume is a received book/gift and Gould’s manuscript is work product; neither is a surviving incoming letter.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier proof exchange with Gray, but no surviving Gray response and no text-specific carryover.
Later nomenclature question in the same Birds project, but not a response to this thanks/request.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Thanks for a volume and requests completion of Gould’s manuscript; no surviving Gray letter is present. The gift and manuscript references demonstrate receipt/possession of objects, not an incoming correspondence prompt.

evidence.quote: the pleasure of thanking you for your very obliging present of your volume of the Genera of Birds
finishing the remaining M.S. for the Birds of Beagles Voyage

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Gray whether a revised ground-woodpecker name, “Chrysoptilus Chilensis G. R. Gray,” is correct, asks him to leave the sheets on returning home, and limits the requested review to that proof.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [Feb 1841] (1841-02-01 through 1841-02-28); exact day unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to George Robert Gray; the revise/sheets are physical proof materials.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Adjacent Birds proof/index request, but different task and no Gray response text.
Earlier specimen and species discussion, but no distinctive wording establishes a direct link.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Specific proof query to Gray with no surviving incoming Gray text. The editorial footnote records the eventual printed treatment, which cannot substitute for Gray’s missing response or establish receipt.

evidence.quote: I have altered this to “Chrysoptilus Chilensis G. R. Gray”
Is this right.?
leave these sheets

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Gray to mark errors in the proof index, promises to send the proof of Gray’s Errata, and asks the bearer to bring back any available bird specimens.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially supplied bounded range [Feb–Mar 1841] (1841-02-01 through 1841-03-31); exact day unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes to George Robert Gray. Proofs and bird specimens are physical materials; “Errata” is a promised proof, not a surviving incoming letter.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same Birds proof project, but the index/Errata task is distinct and no Gray reply survives.
Earlier specimen exchange, but no unique text or date evidence links it as direct antecedent.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Requests proof checking and specimen return; no surviving Gray input is located. A shared production project and bearer route do not identify a direct prompt or establish actual return of specimens.

evidence.quote: looking over the proof of the index
I will send proof of your Errata, soon
If any of the Specimens of Birds are at hand the Bearer may as well bring some back

record_reviews.summary: Darwin orders a large pot of soft spermaceti ointment from an ambiguously identified Baxter chemist.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held bounded range [1842–82?] (1842-01-01 through 1882-12-31), with questioned year component and conjectural addressee William Baxter or W. W. Baxter; no secure day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes a two-paragraph commercial order; no reply or other voice survives, and the ointment is a supplied product.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same ointment and addressee family, but both dates/addressee are conjectural and no response is present.
Another Baxter order, but a different product and unresolved alternative date structure.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone order with no surviving Baxter reply; repeated product wording is insufficient to pair notes. The editorial date/addressee are explicitly conjectural; do not collapse William Baxter and William Walmisley Baxter or infer a year from the product.

evidence.quote: Please send me a large pot of soft spermaceti ointment

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks the Baxter addressee to half fill a bottle with carbonate of ammonia and signs from Down.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative-date record: header “2 [October 1842 – April 1882]”; XML range 1842-10-02 through 1882-03-02 and date_structure alternative_dates. Addressee remains conjectural.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes a terse commercial/medical supply order; the bottle is a physical object and no reply survives.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Another October-numbered Baxter order but different contents; unresolved year/date alternatives prevent sequencing.
Same address convention and missing enclosure, but no identified contents or direct reply.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone order; no incoming Baxter response is located. Do not treat Down residence or the editorially supplied date candidates as proof of posting, receipt or a direct pair.

evidence.quote: Please half fill Bottle with C. of Ammonia
Down | 2d.—

record_reviews.summary: Darwin orders distilled water, two ounces of camphorated spirits and an unspecified bottle of the same perfume from Baxter.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held bounded range [10 October 1842 – April 1882] (1842-10-10 through 1882-04-10); editorially supplied year/day constraints and addressee conjecture remain unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes a terse supply order; products are physical supplies and the source contains no Baxter reply.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same month/day-number form but different product; alternative date candidates make exact sequence unsafe.
Later-looking supply order to the same addressee family but its year is also held and contents differ.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone order with no surviving Baxter input or response. The product notes in footnotes explain possible uses but do not identify a particular transaction date or receipt.

evidence.quote: A big bottle of distilled water
2 oz of Camphorated Spirits
Please fill Bottle with same perfume

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Baxter to read an enclosed note, act on it and send two bottles, saying the note need not be returned. The enclosure and its commission are missing.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative dates: [1842–5 or 1853 or 1855–68?], XML range 1842-10-24 through 1868-10-24; exact year and addressee are conjectural.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes the surviving order; the unidentified enclosure would contain the substantive request and is not available.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Another Baxter supply order, but its contents and date alternatives do not identify the missing enclosure.
Another terse order to the possible same chemists, but no text supplies the two-bottle commission.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Surviving fragment refers to an unlocated enclosure; no Baxter reply or identified contents support a direct pair. The missing enclosure prevents identifying what was ordered; do not infer it from other Baxter notes.

evidence.quote: read the enclosed & act on it, sending my two Bottles
The note need not be returned to me

record_reviews.summary: Darwin orders a large pot of soft spermaceti ointment from the ambiguously identified Baxter addressee and dates the note only “Decr 8th.”
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative-date record [8 December 1842–81] (XML 1842-12-08 through 1881-12-08); editorially supplied year and addressee remain unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes the surviving order; the ointment is a supplied product, not a letter/enclosure.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same product and likely chemist, but both years/addressees are conjectural and no reply survives.
Same supplier family but unrelated spirits-of-wine request with its own held date.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone repeat/order with no Baxter response located. The repeated ointment request supports possible commercial continuity only; it does not establish a direct correspondence pair or exact year.

evidence.quote: a large pot of soft spermaceti ointment
Down. Decr 8th—

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Baxter to fill a bottle with spirits of wine and signs from Down on 16 March.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative-date record [16 March 1843–82] (XML 1843-03-16 through 1882-03-16); editorially supplied year and addressee remain unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes a terse supply order; spirits of wine are a physical preservative supply.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Five days later by day/month form, same addressee family, but different zinc-label ink recipe and both years are held.
Another product order to possible Baxter, but dates overlap broad alternatives and no response exists.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone supply request with no incoming Baxter response. Apparent chronological proximity is not secure because all year candidates are unresolved.

evidence.quote: Please fill Bottle with Spirits of Wine
Down | March 16th.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin gives Baxter a recipe for a bottle of zinc-label ink: powdered verdigris, sal ammoniac, lamp-black and water, then signs on 21 March from Down.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Period-held alternative-date record [21 March 1843–82] (XML 1843-03-21 through 1882-03-21); editorially supplied year and addressee remain unresolved.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin writes the recipe/order; the bottle and chemical mixture are physical supplies. The Herbert reference in the footnote is a published source, not correspondence.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Same day-number series and supplier family, but separate request five days earlier by header form and no reply; held years prevent secure sequencing.
Another bottle order to possible Baxter, but different chemical and broad alternative dates.

record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Standalone chemical order/recipe; no Baxter response survives. The recipe’s published source and probable use do not establish a direct correspondence antecedent or actual fulfilment.

evidence.quote: fill the enclosed Bottle in following proportions
Verdigris in powder [drachm]i
Water [drachm]x

issues.description: All 19 batch-10 target records were read with every retained body paragraph, header text, editorial summary and footnote.
DCP-LETT-559 and all Baxter notes retain period holds/alternative candidates; no hold was relaxed from bracket notation alone.
DCP-LETT-451 contains a bracketed editorial body description with embedded quotations; bracketed paraphrase was not treated as verbatim Darwin voice.
Malcolmson letters contain quoted or reported Ward, Low, Hardie, Allan, Agassiz and other third-party material; those voices are not Darwin prompts.
DCP-LETT-1147 is incomplete, DCP-LETT-1768 lacks its enclosure, and none of the located Gray/Baxter exchanges includes a surviving incoming response.
Additional full reads DCP-LETT-548C and DCP-LETT-660F are John Edward Gray testimonials/coral-specimen administration, distinct from George Robert Gray and unrelated to batch-10 direct pairing.
